samples.question: The grey bars in this picture are pipes. Pipes carry water only along their own length and join only where they actually meet at a junction. The green square is the pump. The red, blue and orange squares are tanks. A route from the pump to a tank is any chain of connected pipes that leads from the green square to that tank. Pipes are drawn with different thicknesses, and water through a route is limited by its narrowest pipe: the capacity of a route is the thickness of the thinnest pipe anywhere along it. Each tank is scored by its best route, that is the route whose narrowest pipe is as thick as possible. How long a route is, how many turns it makes, how many pipes it uses and how far the tank sits from the pump on the page all do not matter. Which tank has the highest-capacity route from the pump? Answer red, blue or orange.
